nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: The as-purchased Ni foam (NF) was washed with acetone three times to remove the organics; the nickel oxides layers were dissolved by sonication for 30 min in 1.0 M HCl and followed by pure water for three times to remove additional HCl.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: washed with acetone three times to remove the organics

unit_operations.name: HCl Sonication
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: nickel oxides layers were dissolved by sonication for 30 min in 1.0 M HCl

unit_operations.name: Water Rinsing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: followed by pure water for three times to remove additional HCl

nodes.source_text: First, the as-purchased Ni foam (NF) was washed with acetone three times... followed by pure water for three times to remove additional HCl.

nodes.name: Solvothermal Treatment
nodes.procedure: The cleaned NF was placed in a 50 mL steel autoclave containing 25 mL ethylene glycol solution with nickel nitrate hexahydrate (0.1 mmol), ammonium metavanadate (0.5 mmol), and urea (0.5 mmol), and heated for solvothermal treatment at 160°C for 12 h.

unit_operations.name: Solvothermal Reaction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: placed in a 50 mL steel autoclave containing 25 mL ethylene glycol solution with nickel nitrate hexahydrate (0.1 mmol), ammonium metavanadate (0.5 mmol), and urea (0.5 mmol), and heated for solvothermal treatment at 160°C for 12 h

nodes.source_text: Second, the cleaned NF was placed in a 50 mL steel autoclave containing 25 mL ethylene glycol solution... heated for solvothermal treatment at 160°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Post-treatment and Drying
nodes.procedure: NF was taken out and immersed into pure water and C₂H₆O three times, respectively, and dried in vacuum for 24 h at 80°C.

unit_operations.name: Water Immersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: immersed into pure water... three times

unit_operations.name: Vacuum Drying

nodes.source_text: Third, NF was taken out and immersed into pure water and C₂H₆O three times, respectively, and dried in vacuum for 24 h at 80°C.

nodes.name: Annealing Treatment
nodes.procedure: NF was placed in a tube furnace with a 95% Ar + 5% H₂ atmosphere and heated at 500°C for 1 h (the heating speed was 5°C min⁻¹; the sample was denoted as Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF).

Tafel slopes... 41.22... mV dec⁻¹
Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF can perform the UOR for 55 h at 200 mA cm⁻²... with negligible (<5%) performance degradation

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF exhibit nanosheets structure with nanoparticles uniformly grown on the nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Figure S1b of the Supporting Information (SI), the SEM images of Ni@C - V₂O₃ / NF exhibit the nanosheets' structure, and the nanoparticles are uniformly grown on the nanosheets...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD peaks belong to V₂O₃ (PDF#34-0187) and Ni (PDF#04-0850), confirming presence of V₂O₃ and Ni in Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S2a, the peaks belong to V₂O₃ (PDF#34-0187) and to Ni (PDF#04-0850), suggesting the presence of V₂O₃ and Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows N-doped-carbon coating structures with carbon layer thickness of 1.192 nm in Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the N-doped-carbon coating structures are detected in Figure 2d, and the carbon layer is 1.192 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows fringe spacing of 0.281 nm (116) plane of V₂O₃ and 0.206 nm (111) facets of Ni, confirming heterostructure formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further investigate the microstructure of Ni@C - V₂O₃ / NF, the HRTEM images (Figure 2b,c) show that the fringe spacing is about 0.281 and 0.206 nm which belong to the (116) crystal plane of V₂O₃ and the (111) facets of Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS indicates homogeneous distribution of Ni, V, C, and N elements in Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS indicates the homogeneous distribution of Ni, V, C, and N (Figure 2f), which is consistent with the XPS characterization results...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows positive shift in Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF relative to Ni/NF and Ni-V₂O₃/NF; V 2p shows negative shift relative to V₂O₃/NF; C 1s peaks at 284.8 eV (C-C), 286.3 eV (C-N), 289.1 eV (C=O); N 1s at 398.4 eV (pyridinic-N), 399.9 eV (pyrrolic-N), 401.8 eV (graphitic-N); V 2p with V⁴⁺ 2p₁/₂ (523.9 eV), V³⁺ 2p₁/₂ (522.9 eV), V⁴⁺ 2p₃/₂ (516.4 eV), V³⁺ 2p₃/₂ (515.4 eV); O 1s V-O at 530.6 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Ni@ C-V₂O₃/NF (Figure 3a), for Ni 2p, there is a positive shift relative to Ni/NF and Ni - V₂O₃ / NF (Table S1), respectively. Moreover, a negative shift is found (in Figure 3b and Table S2) for V 2p of the Ni@C - V₂O₃ / NF, as compared with V₂O₃ / NF... The peaks at 289.1, 284.8, and 286.3 eV belong to C=O, C-C, and C-N bonds, respectively. The N 1s are located at 401.8 (graphitic-N), 399.9 (pyrrolic-N), and 398.4 eV (pyridinic-N)... V 2p and O 1s... fitted with V⁴⁺ 2p₁/₂ (523.9 eV), V³⁺ 2p₁/₂ (522.9 eV), V⁴⁺ 2p₃/₂ (516.4 eV), V³⁺ 2p₃/₂ (515.4 eV), and V-O species (530.6 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 114.41 mF/cm² for Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF (vs 71.70 mF/cm² for Ni-V₂O₃/NF, 17.47 mF/cm² for Ni/NF, 48.51 mF/cm² for V₂O₃/NF, 1.6 mF/cm² for precursors).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S15, the CV is tested in the non-Faradaic (RF) region (10 to 100 mV s⁻¹). As seen, the Cdl of Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF (114.41 mF cm⁻²) is higher than Ni - V₂O₃ / NF (71.70 mF cm⁻²), precursors (1.6 mF cm⁻²), Ni/NF (17.47 mF cm⁻²), and V₂O₃/NF (48.51 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS reveals Ni@C-V₂O₃/NF has the smallest charge transfer resistance Rct among investigated catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S7, the EIS is also employed to study the UOR kinetics of catalysts, and the corresponding results reveal that Ni@C - V₂O₃ / NF has the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct)...
